Add/drop deadline passed: contact your college or school registrar

fact_check.claim: 'Available seats are reserved' means class limited to a population such as A&S juniors

Check for holds first if you cannot enroll at your appointment

Swaps only work into open sections

fact_check.note: Page says you are dropped from all sections of the class you were changing.

fact_check.claim: Student Center waitlist numbers do not reflect actual priority (Bowers)
Bowers PIN priority: department majors, other Bowers majors, everyone else; seniors first within each group
PINs start end of first week of add/drop, go out every other day as space allows, end with add period
PIN by email, non-transferable, typically valid 24 hours; do not submit ticket for waitlist/PIN status
Bowers: swapping into a full discussion automatically drops you from the course; always enroll in a backup course
Application-based courses: professor emails a PIN to accepted students
CS 1000-3000 open first-come first-served, CS 3700 and 3780 majors-only for pre-enrollment; 4000 level majors-only pre-enrollment with waitlists for others
No waitlists for CS 1000, 2000, 3000 level courses (Engineering advising)
fact_check.note: Matches; page says monitor open seats.

fact_check.claim: Physics waitlists open just before pre-enroll window and close at 4pm ET on the day the add period closes
Physics guarantees a spot in PHYS 1110, 1112, 1116, 2210, 2213, 2214, 2217, 2218 only to students who join during pre-enroll
fact_check.note: Course list and pre-enroll condition match, but the guarantee is for Physics and Engineering students; the article omits that condition. 'Joining later is not guaranteed' is the article's inference, not stated.

fact_check.claim: Physics: cannot swap into a full class or section; dropping yourself means you are not added back; do not enroll in conflicting sections
Physics full-section request: email physicsenrollment@cornell.edu with NetID, Cornell ID, conflicting class, required class, advisor contact; specific time/section requests not accepted
BIOMG 1350: use swap because dropping may mean the department cannot re-enroll you
fact_check.note: Page: Biology office will not be able to re-enroll you.

fact_check.claim: Some Engineering (MAE) courses: Sibley Qualtrics form does not guarantee placement
First-year writing seminars: you can enroll in only one
fact_check.note: Page says only to enroll in a seminar with open spots; it does not limit students to one. The 'seminars fill fast' claim is also not on the page.

fact_check.claim: Juniors and seniors may prefer ENGL 2880 or 2860, which can substitute for FWS credit
Tommy Tsai '24 said getting into classes means checking Student Center daily during add/drop
fact_check.note: Quote found; used as attributed student experience, not policy.

fact_check.note: Source: 'a line of fifteen kids trying to talk to the professor after the class'. The article's 'so many people were on the waitlist' framing was not confirmed in the fetched excerpt; soften.

beats_top.why: The #1 result (a Statistics department page; returned 403 on fetch, so unread) and the next results (Bowers registrar, Engineering ENGRC waitlist) are single-department pages; ours combines registrar rules, waitlist checkbox, swap traps and who-to-contact in one flow. Judged from the search snippets and the Bowers page, not the top page itself.
changes: Add a short dated note that Cornell course waitlists are unrelated to the undergraduate admissions waitlist, so searchers landing here from that noise are oriented.
Add the Computer Science detail that CS urges students to pre-enroll in a backup, and mention that both lecture and lab seats must be open, with a link to an official page.
Fix the sourcing slips listed in fixes so no claim goes beyond the cited page.

fixes: Change 'Swaps only work into open sections' to say the registrar calls swapping only into open sections 'best practice', then keep the sentence that checking the waitlist box during a swap drops you from all sections; source https://registrar.cornell.edu/students/enrollment/student-center-help/swapping-sections-within-a-course

In the first-year writing seminar bullet, delete 'seminars fill fast and you can enroll in only one'; replace with 'enroll only in a seminar that has open spots', which is what https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/advising/course-enrollment-challenges/ says.

In the Physics paragraph, say the waitlist guarantee for PHYS 1110, 1112, 1116, 2210, 2213, 2214, 2217 and 2218 applies to Physics and Engineering students who join during their pre-enroll period; delete or label as our inference the sentence 'joining later is not guaranteed'; source https://www.physics.cornell.edu/enrollment-guide

In 'What students report', replace 'so many people were on the waitlist that about fifteen students were trying to reach the professor' with 'described a line of fifteen students trying to talk to the professor after class'; source the Sun article.
